Should you be on Reddit to drive LLM recommendations?

One of Discuss GTM’s chat members shared an unreviewed preprint study I just finished reading. It looks at whether Reddit shapes which brands AI tools recommend – even when the tools don’t cite Reddit.

Sample and methodology:

The author pulled 12K posts and 100K+ comments from 60 subreddits via Reddit’s API.

Brand mentions were scored by upvotes, placement (title, body, comment), and comment depth.

Those scores were then ranked against brand recommendations from ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini across 50 product queries, each asked three times. The correlation analysis spans 12 consumer categories.

A second test compared Reddit citations in 60 API calls (15 queries) vs. 100 web UI queries per platform, collected via browser automation in February 2026.

Key findings:

• Reddit brand rankings and AI brand rankings lined up fairly strongly.
• Web UIs cited Reddit in 44% of queries on Google AI Mode, 20% on Perplexity, and 17% on ChatGPT.
• APIs returned 0% Reddit citations on every platform.
• Opinion and comparison queries pulled in Reddit most often: 70.8% on Google AI Mode and 45.8% on Perplexity.
• Claude cited Reddit zero times in both channels, but it cited any source in only 19% of web UI queries.

Now, how I read it.

Reddit may influence LLM recommendations even when it’s not cited.

The big implication: citation tracking alone may underestimate Reddit’s role. If brand rankings on Reddit correlate with brand recommendations from LLMs, Reddit may function as a background reputation / consensus layer – not just a direct source.

Remember my post about fan-out queries? Here’s the answer for getting into an LLM’s pre-search association brain.

So “being cited” and “shaping the answer” are two different things.

Reddit also seems especially relevant for high-consideration / opinion-heavy queries. So if you’re in a very competitive field and switching costs are high—yeah, you have to think about building a presence on Reddit.

Shilling is also not the answer.

Engagement quality > raw mention volume.

Because the Reddit score included upvotes, title/body placement, and comment depth, the implied signal is a brand showing up in substantive, highly engaged discussions.

Reddit = reputation channel.

I definitely need to research more guerrilla tactics on Reddit. For now, I’m just passively growing karma—but I’m not sure how to inject brand discussions without it becoming shilling / spam.

Feel free to share your ideas.

PS: This study is an unreviewed preprint from a consultancy with a stake in GEO advice, and it’s co-written with Claude folks.

I don’t buy this. 

Yes, the charitable read is that constant attacking/defending leads to an overall more hardened structure. I think everyone can feel how that makes intuitive sense. 

But, I’d draw an analogy between this and Kelly betting. Everyone knows you don’t want to make repeated bets with full risk of ruin. The problem with cybersecurity and cryptocurrency is that due to the irreversible nature of transactions, you’re always in a ”risk of ruin”-like environment. If you have an automated warfare cybersecurity environment, I’d wager that your risk of ruin is actually higher, even if the ”probability of penetration per attempt” is lower. 

The fact that every possible exploit at every protocol at all times is constantly attempted… across the whole stack, at every layer… like, it’s possible that some Lindy applications like the Bitcoin baselayer would be more secure in this way. But for anything dynamic that goes through changes (e.g. Lightning, anything smart contract/upgradeable layer) the chance of an irreversible fault overall seems higher.

2. The development could provide Samsung and SK Hynix with greater long-term revenue visibility and reinforces the structural demand outlook for the broader memory industry, including Micron $MU.

4. Meta $META has reportedly upsized its Class A common stock offering to $25B from $22.5B, pricing the shares at $625 each as the company raises additional capital to support its massive AI infrastructure expansion. Notably, NVIDIA $NVDA is investing $3B in the offering, while AMD $AMD is committing another $1B, giving two of Meta's major AI chip suppliers direct equity exposure to one of their largest customers. The expanded offering highlights Meta's increasingly aggressive capital-raising strategy as it prepares to spend $135B–$145B on capital expenditures in 2026. The participation of NVIDIA and AMD also underscores the growing financial interconnectedness of the AI ecosystem, with semiconductor suppliers investing directly in the hyperscalers purchasing their hardware.

5. Qualcomm $QCOM and Anduril are teaming up to launch BlueChip, a new venture focused on manufacturing rugged, waterproof, American-made laptops for the U.S. military, government agencies, law enforcement, and first responders, according to the Wall Street Journal. The devices will be assembled at Anduril's Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio and powered by Qualcomm Snapdragon X processors manufactured by TSMC in Arizona. Anduril founder Palmer Luckey said approximately 90% of the planned components already come from the U.S. and allied countries, with the long-term goal of producing the entire laptop domestically, including displays and other components currently sourced overseas. The initiative prioritizes secure computing, fully traceable supply chains, and reduced dependence on foreign manufacturing for national-security applications. The first laptops are expected in 2027, with pricing estimated at roughly 20% above conventional high-end PCs.

6. President Donald Trump made two major statements, reiterating his administration's decision to replace the terms “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” with “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official executive-branch communications, following a September executive order. Separately, Trump suggested that Venezuela could eventually become the 51st U.S. state, floating the possibility of replacing its presidency with a governorship during remarks in Corpus Christi, Texas. Trump also celebrated the U.S. military intervention in Venezuela and its subsequent oil agreement, describing the operation as a historic victory and highlighting expanded American access to Venezuelan oil reserves.

7. Tesla $TSLA rallied approximately 4% on Tuesday to $407.46, extending Monday's 5.2% gain as shares broke above key technical resistance levels. The rally was primarily fueled by Barclays upgrading Tesla to Overweight and raising its price target to $450 from $370, citing improving automotive demand, accelerating energy storage growth, and a potential merger with SpaceX $SPCX that could create a premium for Tesla shareholders. Meanwhile, Tesla's robotaxi expansion continues to gain momentum, with its Texas fleet reportedly exceeding 1,050 vehicles, Cybercabs outnumbering Model Ys, and additional service areas planned, including Dallas. Investors are also responding to improving FSD adoption, strong demand for energy storage from AI data centers, and signs of stabilization in Tesla's core automotive business. 

8. Brazil's stock market experienced an extraordinary selloff on October 26, with the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF $EWZ plunging 19.8% in a single session, representing an estimated 8.4-standard-deviation move based on its historical daily volatility. Over the past 20 years, EWZ has averaged a daily return of approximately 0.04%, with a standard deviation of 2.36%, making Monday's decline an extreme statistical outlier. Under a theoretical normal distribution, a move of this magnitude would have an exceptionally small probability, illustrating just how unusual the selloff was relative to historical volatility. However, actual financial markets exhibit fat-tailed return distributions, meaning extreme declines occur more frequently than conventional statistical models predict. The plunge highlights the severity of the selling pressure in Brazilian equities and the risks associated with sudden market shocks.

9. Alphabet's $GOOGL Waymo is expanding its fully autonomous ride-hailing service by nearly 250 square miles across five existing U.S. markets over the next week, further accelerating its commercial robotaxi rollout. In Los Angeles, Waymo is extending service along the coast into the South Bay, including Torrance, while San Diego coverage will expand north to La Jolla, connecting riders to UC San Diego, the VA, and University Town Center. In Nashville, the company is expanding south to include Nashville Zoo, while Orlando will see its eastern service area nearly double alongside improved downtown coverage. The San Francisco Bay Area will also gain additional southern coverage, including a connection to Berryessa BART Station. The expansion increases Waymo's geographic reach and the number of destinations accessible to existing riders, rather than representing launches in five new cities, as Alphabet continues scaling its autonomous transportation network.

10. 11. Amazon $AMZN is reportedly working to reduce its reliance on Anthropic's AI models as the cost of operating Alexa+ continues to climb, according to Business Insider. Internal projections estimated that Alexa+ cloud computing expenses could reach approximately $1.7B in 2026, nearly triple the prior year's costs, prompting Amazon to explore routing more AI requests through its own lower-cost models and infrastructure. The company also considered delaying or scaling back Moonraker, its advanced AI agent initiative, which was projected to require more than $100M in GPU spending this year. The developments highlight the growing pressure on major technology companies to improve AI inference economics, reduce dependence on third-party model providers, and balance increasingly expensive AI capabilities with sustainable profitability.

12. U.S. stock market breadth is improving significantly, with the S&P 500 Equal-Weight Index outperforming the traditional market-cap-weighted S&P 500 by 4.0 percentage points in October, putting it on track for its second-strongest monthly relative performance since April 2009. The equal-weight index has gained 4.3% this month, compared with just 0.3% for the S&P 500, marking a sharp reversal from September, when equal-weight stocks underperformed by 4.7 percentage points, their worst relative month since March 2020. For comparison, the equal-weight index outperformed by 4.2 percentage points in April. Year-to-date, the Equal-Weight Index is up 13.4% versus 12.1% for the S&P 500, suggesting market leadership is broadening beyond the largest technology and AI companies as more sectors and individual stocks participate in the rally.

This article is full of blatant misinformation.  

"The components Luckey specified that are planned to be American-made from the start are the display glass, the frame around the display, and parts of the ribbon component." 

No.  That is not what I said.  This was a response to a specific question about the display modules in the current prototype vs the final product.  As I explicitly said, BlueChip has American chips, batteries, metallics, plastics, glass, etc, and we have a clear technical roadmap to 100% American components. 

"It sounds like BlueChip’s first laptop will be well below the 65-percent requirement to count as American-made" 

This is nuts.  There is a reason no other reporter has came to this conclusion.  One hint might be the extended discussion we had explicitly about the government requirements for American-made hardware and why meeting that bar is so important.

"Palmer Luckey is of course a controversial figure, with his history of fueling right wing troll farms" 

This never happened.  You are pushing a lie The Verge has pushed for over a decade now.  Yes, you have written a bunch of stories claiming this happened, but it just ain't so.  I gave $9,000 to a group that ran a single anti-Clinton billboard.  The "right wing troll farms" narrative was a fabricated story pushed shortly before the 2016 election because Dems desperately wanted a right-wing equivalent to the actually-real Correct The Record, an online astroturfing organization that paid people to troll and "correct" Trump supporters online.  

But there was no such thing.  It was all disinformation.  Which is why most of the stories about it were later deleted.  Yet here you are, lying again.
